## 1. Identification Strategy
Difference-in-differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects: subsidised markets versus the
rest, before versus after period 4. Key assumption: parallel trends in log revenue.

## 2. R Code
```r
# SYNTHETIC fixture completion: '# OUT:' lines are echoed by the test stand-in for Rscript
library(fixest)
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s901_data.csv")
m <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df)
# OUT:DID coef: -0.2851
print(summary(m))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect a negative effect: a decrease in log revenue of about -0.3 in subsidised
markets, i.e. a decline relative to control markets.
